instruction.text: Select the circuit with the dimmer bulbs.

atoms.a: What is different about the circuit with dimmer bulbs?

atoms.b: Although wires transfer ((++electricity light)) well, the longer they are, the ((++further shorter)) the electricity has to travel to complete the circuit.
This means that ((++less more)) electricity is able to reach the bulbs, making them dimmer.
This is referred to as resistance, a measure of how hard it is for ((++electricity plastic)) to travel round a circuit.

atoms.a: Other than the brightness of the bulbs, is there a visible difference between the two circuits?

feedback.end: Although it is not obvious from looking at the wires, the circuit on the left uses resistance wires.

atoms.b: Resistance wires are designed ((++differently the_same_way)) to normal wires: they are made to resist the flow of electricity. When using resistance wires, increasing the length of wire will ((++heavily barely)) affect the brightness of bulbs or volume of buzzers.

text: An everyday example of resistance wires can be found in toasters. By resisting the flow of electricity, electrical energy is converted into heat energy, and the hot wires toast your bread!
